title: Lagrangian–Eulerian learning of flow field and trajectories with TrajectoryFlowNet - Nature Machine Intelligence
text:
A preprint version of the article is available at arXiv.

AbstractPredicting particle transport in complex flows is traditionally achieved by solving the Navier–Stokes equations. Numerical and experimental methods typically require deep physical insights and incur high computational costs. Although machine learning offers an alternative, existing approaches fail to generalize the prediction of long-range particle trajectories in sparse data regimes. Here, to this end, we propose TrajectoryFlowNet, a Lagrangian–Eulerian physics-informed neural network architecture, for fluid flow velocimetry and imaging via learning to predict spatiotemporal flow fields and long-range particle trajectories. The salient features of our model include its ability to handle complex flow patterns with irregular boundaries, predict the full-field flows, image the long-range flow trajectory of any arbitrary particle, and ensure physical consistency in predictions based on only scarce measurement of flow trajectories. We validate TrajectoryFlowNet via both numerical examples (for example, lid-driven cavity flow and complex cylinder flow) and experimental test cases (for example, aortic and ventricle blood flows) across diverse flow scenarios. The results demonstrate our model’s effectiveness in capturing intricate particle-laden flow dynamics, enabling long-range tracking of particles and accurate construction of flow fields in real-world applications.

Data availability

All the used datasets (the synthetic lid-driven cavity flow data, the synthetic complex cylinder flow data, the experimental aortic blood-flow data and the experimental left-ventricle blood-flow data) in this study are available via GitHub at https://github.com/WanJingdi/TrajectoryFlowNet (ref. 69). Source data are provided with this paper.
Code availability

All the source codes to reproduce the results in this study are available via GitHub at https://github.com/WanJingdi/TrajectoryFlowNet (ref. 69).
